text: This story owns no legacy criterion identifier and keeps the legacy behaviour instead: the eleven criteria AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E1-002 are reworked into eleven new criteria tagged (new, D-RCV-60) that keep the legacy values, columns, messages and test-case mapping, and the eleven legacy test identifiers TC-E1-002-01 to TC-E1-002-11 are kept unchanged at component and contract level.
why: The legacy story states its criteria as AC1 to AC11 inside one feature file with no story-scoped identifier to copy, the WP lists no legacy AC for this story, and its disposition is Split (rework), so the target criteria must be written new while the tested behaviour stays the legacy behaviour.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-002 section 7 (AC1 to AC11) and section 16 (TC-E1-002-01 to -11); Template and Rules R7.2 s7 and s16
confirm: Service owner of rwb-case and the test lead at the story review.
impact: If a legacy identifier must be cited verbatim, eleven scenario tags change and no test, value or rule changes.

text: The list answers one CaseListRow per open case with caseId, caseNo, productGroup, stageCode, status, ownerUserId, queueCode, teamCode, routeCode, entryDate and the account keys of the case, plus accountNumber, totalBalance, daysPastDue, lastContactAt, lastActionCode, dataAsOf, refreshedAt and stale, and rwb-case reads the account and freshness answers of RWB-P1-E1015-CON for one page itself: the account read carries the key list of the page where the contract publishes its batch form and one account key otherwise, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker.
why: The legacy list is one row per case account, the target API publishes one page of cases, Architecture v5 slide 10 puts the merge of case and account answers in gateway-bff, FSD A1.5 puts the account read beside the case list, and DP-05 sends ACE data through the source-data contract, so the row shape and the caller of the account read need one stated answer.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-002 sections 4, 7 (AC2) and 12; API Specification v4 GET /cases and the Case schema; FSD P3 v4 A1.5 and A2.19; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 10; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05, DP-11, DP-19
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-source-data owner in the baseline review of RWB-P1-E1015-CON.
impact: If the merge stays at the edge, two consumed rows, the SourceDataClient and the AC2 assertion move to RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the list operation loses its account columns.

text: refreshedAt is the time the read answered and is carried on every row and on the page, dataAsOf is the ACE business date of the freshness answer and is carried in the header X-Data-As-Of, and a date whose ALS batch is not complete is served with the last complete date and a stale flag rather than refused; no stored build time and no list snapshot exist in the target.
why: The legacy rows carried the refresh time of the nightly build and the list was replaced per business date, while the target list is read from the rows per request and no source says what a refresh time means without a build.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-002 sections 4 (step 10), 7 (AC3, AC5), 8 (BR5) and 13; API Specification v4 GET /cases description (response header X-Data-As-Of); FSD P3 v4 A1.4 (freshness from v_ace_batch_status)
confirm: Service owner of rwb-case with the data steward at the story review.
impact: If a stored build time is required, one stamp row and one day-open write are added; the page header, the refresh line and the AC3 assertion change and nothing else.

text: case.entry.dpd 90, recon.caselist.tolerance.pct 0.00 and caselist.allocation.wait.until 07:15 stay parameter rows with the version in force, the four list values stay reference rows, the page size is bounded at 1 to 200 as API-P3-001 states, the wait time drives the cron of rwb-case-caselist-daily, and the rwb_case login name is taken from the platform naming rule at deployment rather than fixed here.
why: The legacy story names the three parameters and the lists but gives no field identifier for them, and the per-service login has no name in any source, so each value needs one stated home and one stated default.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-002 sections 3, 4 step 8, 8 (BR4, BR5) and 13; API Specification v4 GET /cases (size 1 to 200); context pack P3 (schema rwb_case, one login per service); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-02, DP-06, DP-07
confirm: Business owner for the threshold and the wait time, and the platform DB owner for the login name.
impact: A parameter or list change is a row change with no code release; a login change is a deployment value.

text: Under DP-17 the case list is not a file: case_list_row, its UNIQUE (business_date) key and its replacement unique key, the extract file case-list/<businessDate>.csv, the lake path, the outbound file adapter and the Power BI data set 'Case list v1' are dropped, the reconciliation REC-01 and the orphan check REC-05 stay with JOB-04 in rwb-source-data (RWB-P1-E1011), and the reporting read model is built in rwb-reporting from the events of rwb.case.events.v1.
why: DP-17 removes the data lake and reporting reads events, while the legacy story's build, its publish status, its two checks and its data set are lake artifacts that no target source re-homes; leaving them unowned would leave a story that writes a table nobody owns and a file nobody reads.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-002 sections 4 (steps 9 and 10), 5 (X5), 7 (AC9), 8 (BR7), 12 and 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17 and R3 default ruling; Architecture v5 slide 8 (INT-19 and INT-20 removed)
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-reporting owner at the story review.
impact: If a list extract is still needed, one export operation, one file owner and one access-log entry are added; the read path, the row and the contract stay as published.

text: The four dependency rows of the metadata table stay None as the WP fixes them, and the platform contract rows of the DP table (RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are library and route baselines pulled by the rwb-case platform stories, so this story starts on Day 1 with no build dependency and holds no contract, integration or external dependency of its own.
why: The WP fixes H, C, I and X as empty and Ready to start as Day 1, while six DP rows of the story name a platform baseline each; both facts must stand in one document without inventing a dependency or a lane position.
read: WP B2-P3-012 story line (H, C, I, X empty; ready Day 1; lane L-P3-B); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15, DP-19 and R5.7 rule 8
confirm: Coordinator at the stage check, with the platform library owner.
impact: If the platform baselines are read as build dependencies, the ready-to-start value and six metadata rows change; no story content, test or contract changes.

text: The feature switch keeps the legacy name rwb.p1.case-list and is carried as a platform feature flag: off, GET /cases answers 404 and the Schedule rwb-case-caselist-daily is paused, while the parameters and the lists are still read.
why: The legacy story names the flag rwb.p1.case-list and its off behaviour, and the platform flag library replaces the local property without any source giving a new name, so the legacy name is kept rather than invented.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-002 section 13 (feature flag rwb.p1.case-list); context pack P3 naming rules; Template and Rules R5.5 (no DP row for flags)
confirm: Platform library owner at the story review.
impact: A rename is one flag key and one values-file line; no code path, contract or test data changes.
